en: 7. The Chapter on Latent Dispositions (Anusayayamaka) 7.2 The Great Section (Mahāvāra) 7.2.1.
The Section on Latent Dispositions (Anusayavāra)
7.2.1.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, in him does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie? Yes.
Or else, in whom the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, in him does the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie? Yes.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit also underlie in them? Yes.
Or rather, in whom the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie in them?

In the non-returner, the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie in him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to views also underlie in that person?

In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, but the underlying tendency to views does not underlie in them. In a worldling (*puthujjana*), both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to views underlie.
Or, in whom the underlying tendency to views underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie in that person? Yes, it does.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to doubt also underlie in them?

In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie in them. In the worldling (*puthujjana*), both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie.
Or, in whom the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie in them? Yes, it does.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to existence underlie them? Yes.
Or rather, in whom the underlying tendency to existence underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie them?

In a non-returner, the underlying tendency to existence underlies, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to existence and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie in them? Yes.
Or, in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie in them?

In a non-returner, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie in him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie.
In whom the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, in him the underlying tendency to conceit also underlies? Yes.
Or conversely, in whom the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, in him the underlying tendency to aversion also underlies?

In a non-returner, the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie in him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie.
In whom the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya) ... pe ...

the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) underlie in them? In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie in them. In an ordinary worldling (puthujjana), both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie.
Or again, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie them? Yes.
For whom the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence … [and so on] … the underlying tendency to ignorance underlie them? Yes.
Or again, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie them?

In the non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) underlies, but the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) does not underlie him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie.
Does the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*)... [and] the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) underlie one in whom the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*) underlies?

In three types of persons, the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie them. In the worldling (*puthujjana*), both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit underlie them? Yes.
For whom the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence ... [and so on] ... the underlying tendency to ignorance underlie them? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit underlie them? Yes.
Does the underlying tendency to views underlie that in which the underlying tendency to doubt underlies? Yes.
Or rather, does the underlying tendency to views underlie that in which the underlying tendency to doubt underlies? Yes.
Does the underlying tendency to views underlie that in which the underlying tendency to lust for existence … pe … the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya) underlie them?

For three types of persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendency to views does not underlie them. For the worldling (puthujjana), both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to views underlie.

For whom the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya)… [and so on] … the underlying tendency to ignorance underlie them? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) also underlie?

For three types of persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie them. For the worldling (puthujjana), both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie.
For whom the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence also underlie them? Yes. (End of the section based on a single root.
For whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit also underlie them? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also underlie them?

In a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*) underlies, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) and aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) do not underlie him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion underlie.

Does the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*) …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) underlie that person in whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion underlie?
In two types of persons, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion underlie, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie them.

[The latent tendency] underlies. In an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), both the latent tendency of sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) and the latent tendency of aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) underlie, and the latent tendency of doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) also underlies.
Now, does that in which the latent tendency of doubt underlies also have the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion underlying it? Yes.

And does that in which the latent tendencies of sensual lust and aversion underlie also have the latent tendency of lust for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) … [and so on] … the latent tendency of ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) underlying it? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and to aversion also underlie them?
In the case of a non-returner, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and to aversion do not underlie him.
In the case of three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and to aversion underlie them. (The Section Based on Pairs.)

In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, in him does the underlying tendency to views … pe … the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent?

In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent, yet in them the underlying tendency to doubt does not lie latent.
In an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion [lie latent]...

In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit persist, does the underlying tendency to doubt also persist? Yes. Or, in whom the underlying tendency to doubt persists, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also persist? Yes.
In whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit persist, does the underlying tendency to existence, ... pe ... the underlying tendency to ignorance also persist? Yes.

Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), and conceit (mānānusaya) also underlie?
In the case of a non-returner (anāgāmī), the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit underlie, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie.
In three types of persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, and the underlying tendency to sensual lust...
And the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to conceit underlie [the mind]. (Based on the triad.

In one for whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views underlie, does the underlying tendency to doubt also underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, in one for whom the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views also underlie? Yes.

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence …pe… the underlying tendency to ignorance underlie? Yes.
Or, for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views underlie?
In the case of a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit underlie, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not.

The underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to views underlie it. In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit underlie it, but the underlying tendency to views does not underlie it for them.

In a worldling, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views all underlie it.
And they persist. (The section based on the fourfold root.

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt persist, does the underlying tendency to existence ... pe ... the underlying tendency to ignorance persist for him? Yes.

Or conversely, for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance persists, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt persist for him?

In a non-returner (anāgāmī), the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) and the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) persist, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya),
aversion (paṭighānusaya), views (diṭṭhānusaya), and doubt (vicikicchānusaya) do not persist.
In two types of persons, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, sensual lust, aversion, and conceit persist, but [the others do not].

In them, the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent. In an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, and doubt also lie latent.
(The pentad-based section.)

In one for whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, in one for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence also underlie?
In a non-returner, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, conceit, and lust for existence underlie, but [the others] do not.
The underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie [the mind].
In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit,
and the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlie [the mind], but the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt do not underlie them.

In an ordinary person (*puthujjana*), the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) underlies [the mind], and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*), aversion (*paṭighānusaya*), conceit (*mānānusaya*), views (*diṭṭhānusaya*), doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*), and lust for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) also underlie it. (The Sixfold Root. 7.2.1.2.
Positive Plane (*anuloma-okāsa*).
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie there? No.
Or else, where the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie there? No.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit underlie there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya) also underlie there?

In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie there. In the two feelings of the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya)… [and so on] …the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) also underlie there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie there?
In painful feeling, in the form element, and in the formless element, the underlying tendency to doubt underlies there, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie there.
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm, the underlying tendency to doubt...
And it underlies [the mind], and the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlies it.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to existence also underlie there? No.
Or, where the underlying tendency to existence underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie there? No.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also underlie there?
In painful feeling, in the form element, and in the formless element, the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies there, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not.

The underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies [it]. In two feelings within the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), here both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie.
Wherever the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit underlie there? No.
Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there? No.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent, do the underlying tendency to views … pe … the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there?
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), and in the form-sphere (rūpadhātu) and formless-sphere (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) lies latent;

however, the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) does not lie latent there. In painful feeling (dukkhā vedanā), both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlie there? No.
Or, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlies, does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie there? No.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion underlies, does the underlying tendency to ignorance underlie there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to aversion also lie latent there?

In the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), and in the fine-material sphere (rūpadhātu) and immaterial sphere (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there.
In painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and [the underlying tendency to aversion] lie latent.
And the underlying tendency to aversion underlies it.
Wherever the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, does the underlying tendency to views ... pe ... the underlying tendency to doubt underlie there? Yes.
Or else, wherever the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to conceit underlie there?
In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not lie latent there.
In the two types of feeling within the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), and in the fine-material and immaterial realms (rūpadhātu and arūpadhātu),
both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent.
Where the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) lies latent, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) also lie latent there?

In the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent, but the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not lie latent there. In the form-sphere realm (rūpadhātu) and the formless-sphere realm (arūpadhātu), both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to lust for existence lie latent.
Or conversely, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence lies latent, does the underlying tendency to conceit also lie latent there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, there the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies? Yes.
Or else, where the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, there the underlying tendency to conceit underlies?
In the case of painful feeling, here the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie there. In the realm of sensual desire...
In two types of feeling—the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—herein, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent.
Wherever the underlying tendency to views lies latent, does the underlying tendency to doubt also lie latent there? Yes.
Or conversely, wherever the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent, does the underlying tendency to views also lie latent there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya) underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) also underlie there?

In the three feelings of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to views underlies, but the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie there. In the fine-material realm (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial realm (arūpadhātu), both the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlie.
Or conversely, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlies, does the underlying tendency to views also underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to views underlies, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie there? Yes.
Or, conversely, where the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, does the underlying tendency to views also underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence also underlie there?

In the three feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) underlies there, but the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) does not underlie there.
In the fine-material sphere (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial sphere (arūpadhātu), both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlie there.
Or, wherever the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlies, does the underlying tendency to doubt also underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, there the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies? Yes.
Or else, where the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, there the underlying tendency to doubt underlies? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlies, there the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies? Yes.
Or again, where the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence lie latent there?
In the three feelings of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent, but the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not lie latent there.
In the fine-material realm (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial realm (arūpadhātu), both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to lust for existence lie latent.
It underlies. (The section based on one root.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit also underlie there? No.
Or else, where the underlying tendency to conceit underlies, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion also underlie there?
In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent there,

but the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there. In two types of feeling within the sense-sphere element, the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust lie latent there,
but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) and the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) underlie, does the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*) ... [and so on] ... the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) underlie there?
No. Or, conversely, where the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie there?
In the fine-material element (*rūpadhātu*) and the immaterial element (*arūpadhātu*), the underlying tendency to doubt underlies, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not.

And the underlying tendency to aversion also underlies them. In two types of feeling within the sense-sphere realm, the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie them, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie them there.
In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie it, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie it there.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence also underlie there? No.
Or conversely, where the underlying tendency to existence underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also underlie there? No.
Where the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie there? No.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya) and aversion (paṭighānusaya) also underlie there?

In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie there.
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to sensual lust [underlie].

And the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies it, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie it there. In regard to painful feeling, both the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie it, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie it there. (The Section Based on Pairs.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit underlie, does the underlying tendency to views ... pe ... the underlying tendency to doubt underlie there? There is none.

Or, where the underlying tendency of doubt (vicikicchānusaya) underlies, do the underlying tendencies of sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), and conceit (mānānusaya) also underlie there?

In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendencies of doubt and conceit underlie, but the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and aversion do not underlie there.
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), however...
The underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there,
but the underlying tendency to aversion does not lie latent there. In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there,
but the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit do not lie latent there.

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*), the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*), and the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*) underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) underlie there?
No. Or, conversely, wherever the underlying tendency to existence underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit underlie there?

In the fine-material element (*rūpadhātu*) and the immaterial element (*arūpadhātu*), the underlying tendencies to existence and conceit underlie, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie there.
Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also underlie there?
No. Or, wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also underlie there?
In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendencies to ignorance and conceit underlie, but [the others] do not underlie there.

The underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie [the mind]. In two types of feeling within the sense-sphere realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit underlie [the mind], but the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie there.
In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie [the mind], but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie there.
and the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) persist. (Based on the triad.

Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya), the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya), the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya) persist, does the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) persist there?

No. Or else, where the underlying tendency to doubt persists, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views persist there?
In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views lie latent;
however, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not lie latent there.

In the two feelings of the sense-sphere element, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views [lie latent].

The underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie it. In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendencies to doubt, aversion, and views underlie it, but the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit do not underlie it there.
Wherever the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence underlie there? No.

Or, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) underlies, do the underlying tendencies to lust for sense-pleasures (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), conceit (mānānusaya), and views (diṭṭhānusaya) also underlie there?

In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendencies to lust for existence, conceit, and views underlie; but the underlying tendencies to lust for sense-pleasures and aversion do not underlie there.
Where the underlying tendencies to lust for sense-pleasures, aversion, conceit, and views underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) also underlie there? There is none.

Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), conceit (mānānusaya), and views (diṭṭhānusaya) also underlie there?
In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendencies to ignorance, conceit, and views underlie;
however, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie there. In the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), with respect to two types of feeling...
Herein, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views underlie;

yet the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie there. In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views underlie;
yet the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit do not underlie there. (The section based on the fourfold root.)

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence also underlie there?

In that same person, within the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), and in the fine-material realm (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial realm (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent there; however, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not lie latent there for them.

The latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of views do not underlie it for those two types of persons in the fine-material element and the immaterial element;
nor do the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of views, and the latent tendency of doubt underlie it for them there.

And they persist. In those very persons, within the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit persist there;
yet the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt do not persist for them there. In those very persons, within painful feeling...
In them, the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent there;
however, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, conceit, views, and doubt do not lie latent in them there.
In an ordinary person within the form element or the formless element, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, conceit, views, and doubt [lie latent there].
And they do not underlie it; yet, for that person, in two types of feeling within the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust,
the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie it, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie it there.
The underlying tendency to aversion underlies it. In that same person, regarding that painful feeling, the underlying tendencies to ignorance, aversion, views, and doubt underlie it;
however, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and conceit do not underlie it in that regard. (The section based on the pentad.)

In whomsoever the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for existence lie latent in a particular sphere, does the underlying tendency to ignorance also lie latent in that person in that same sphere?

No. Or conversely, in whomsoever the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent in a particular sphere, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence also lie latent in that person in that same sphere?
In an Anāgāmī, regarding painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) underlies that [feeling] there;

however, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), conceit (mānānusaya), views (diṭṭhānusaya), doubt (vicikicchānusaya), and lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) do not underlie it there.
For that same person, regarding the two feelings in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu)...

In that case, the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) and the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*) underlie it, but for that person, in that state, the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*),
aversion (*paṭighānusaya*), views (*diṭṭhānusaya*), doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*), and lust for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) do not underlie it. For that same person,
in the form element (*rūpadhātu*) and the formless element (*arūpadhātu*), the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to conceit [underlie it].

and the underlying tendency to attachment to existence (bhavarāgānusaya) underlie it; yet, for him, the underlying tendencies to sensual desire (kāmarāgānusaya), aversion (paṭighānusaya), views (diṭṭhānusaya), and doubt (vicikicchānusaya) do not underlie it there.

For two types of persons—in the fine-material sphere (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial sphere (arūpadhātu)—the underlying tendencies to ignorance (avijjānusaya), conceit (mānānusaya), and attachment to existence (bhavarāgānusaya) underlie it there, but for them...
In that regard, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent.

In those same persons, within the two types of feeling in the sense-sphere realm, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, and the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent;
however, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt do not lie latent there for them.

And the underlying tendency to lust for existence underlies [them]. In those same persons, when there is painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance and the underlying tendency to aversion underlie it;

but the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for existence do not underlie it. In the case of the worldling...
In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendencies of ignorance, conceit, views, doubt, and lust for existence lie latent in that person there;
however, the underlying tendencies of sensual lust and aversion do not lie latent in him there.
In the case of that same person, in two types of feeling within the sense-sphere element...

In that case, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt underlie it;
however, the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to lust for existence do not underlie it for that person there.
For that same person, in regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views [underlie it].
The latent tendency of doubt persists there, but the latent tendencies of sensual lust, pride, and lust for existence do not persist there for him.
(End of the Sixfold Root. This concludes the positive sequence in the Chapter on Latent Tendencies.
7.2.1.4. Negative Person (Paṭilomapuggala) In one for whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie? Yes.
Or, in one for whom the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust not underlie? Yes.
For whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie?

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie for him. For an arahant, both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to conceit do not underlie. Or conversely:
for whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie? Yes.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not lie latent, in him the underlying tendency to views … pe … the underlying tendency to doubt does not lie latent? Yes.
Or else, in whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not lie latent, in him the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not lie latent?

In two types of persons the underlying tendency to doubt does not lie latent, yet the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not lie latent in them. In two other types of persons neither the underlying tendency to doubt nor the underlying tendency to sensual lust lies latent.
In whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to existence … [and so on] … does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie?

In a non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie in him. In an arahant, both the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ignorance do not underlie.
Or, conversely, in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie? Yes.
In whom the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) does not underlie?

In the non-returner (anāgāmī), the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie in him. In the Arhat (arahant), both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to conceit do not underlie.
Or, conversely, in whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie? Yes, it does.
For whom the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to views … [and so on] … the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie?

For two types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, yet for them the underlying tendency to aversion does not fail to underlie. For two other types of persons, neither the underlying tendency to doubt nor the underlying tendency to aversion underlies.
In whom the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to lust for existence... [and so on] ...does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie?

In the non-returner, the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie in him. In the Arhat, both the underlying tendency to aversion and the underlying tendency to ignorance do not underlie. Or conversely:
in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, in him the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie? Yes, it does.
For whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to views... [and so on] ...the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie?

For three types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, yet for them the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie. For an Arahant, neither the underlying tendency to doubt nor the underlying tendency to conceit underlies.

For whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to lust for existence ... [and so on] ... the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie? Yes.
For whom the underlying tendency to views does not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to views does not underlie? Yes. For whom the underlying tendency to views ... [as before] ...
the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, for that person the underlying tendency to lust for existence ... [as before] ... the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie?

In three types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, yet for them the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie. In an Arahant, both the underlying tendency to doubt and the underlying tendency to ignorance do not underlie.
Or, for whomsoever the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie that person? Yes.
For whomsoever the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie that person? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence not underlie that person? Yes. (Based on a single root.)
For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie for them?

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie for them. For an arahant, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, and the underlying tendency to conceit also does not underlie.
Or conversely, for one in whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie for them? Yes.

For whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, for that person does the underlying tendency to views ... pe ... the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie? Yes.
Or else, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, for that person do the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie?
For two types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie; yet for them, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion [may still] underlie.

And they do not underlie. For two types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, and the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie.

Is it the case that for whichever person the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, the underlying tendency to existence … pe … and the underlying tendency to ignorance do not underlie?

For a non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, but the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie him. For an arahant, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, and the underlying tendency to ignorance also does not underlie.

Or, for whom the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) and aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) also not underlie them? Yes. (End of the Section Based on Two Roots.

For whom the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit (*mānānusaya*) do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*) ... [and so on] ... up to ... the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) also not underlie them? Yes.
Or, for whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit also not underlie them?
In two types of persons, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, yet the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, and conceit do not fail to underlie them.
In a non-returner, the underlying tendencies to doubt, sensual lust, and aversion do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie him.
In an arahant, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie...
The underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit do not underlie [in this person].

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence … pe … the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie? Yes.

Or conversely, for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie? Yes. (Based on the Triplet.)

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, and the underlying tendency to views do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie for them? Yes.
Or conversely, for one in whom the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust, aversion, conceit, and views not underlie for them?
For two types of persons, the underlying tendencies to doubt and views do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to sensual lust [does] not [necessarily] not underlie for them.
In the non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views do not underlie;
yet it is not that the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie for him.

In the arahant, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, and the underlying tendency to views do not underlie, nor does the underlying tendency to conceit.
And they do not underlie... [as above] ... (Based on the fourfold root.

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence... [as above] ...the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie him? Yes.

Or else, for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, and the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie him? Yes. (Based on the fivefold root.)

For one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for existence do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie? Yes.

Or rather, for one in whom the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, do the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, and the underlying tendency to lust for existence not underlie? Yes. (The Section Based on the Sixfold Root.)
7.2.1.5. Negative Order (Paṭiloma-okāsa) Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie there?
In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not fail to underlie there.

In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu), the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), and the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya) nor the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) underlies.
Or, where the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie?
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not [thereby] cease to underlie.

It does not underlie. In the fine-material element, the immaterial element, and the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to aversion nor the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies there.
Is it the case that wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie there?

In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie there, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie there. In painful feeling and in the unconditioned, neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust nor the underlying tendency to conceit underlies there.
Or again: Where the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya) does not underlie?

Yes. Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya)... [and so on] ...the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) does not underlie?
In painful feeling, in the form element, and in the formless element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie; yet it is not the case that there...
The underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie it. In the unperturbed [states], neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust nor the underlying tendency to doubt underlies it.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie it, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust not underlie it there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie it, does the underlying tendency to existence not underlie it there?
In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to existence does not fail to underlie there.
In painful feeling and in the unincluded [dhammas], neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust nor the underlying tendency to existence underlies.
Or else, wherever the underlying tendency to existence does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust also not underlie there?

In two feelings of the sense-sphere (*kāmadhātu*), the underlying tendency to craving for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) does not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) does not fail to underlie there.
In painful feeling and in the unconditioned (*apariyāpanna*), neither the underlying tendency to craving for existence nor the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies.
Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) not underlie there?

In painful feeling, in the form element, and in the formless element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not underlie there, yet the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie there.
In the unperturbed (the supramundane), neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust nor the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies there.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust not underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie there?

In the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), and in the form-sphere realm (rūpadhātu) and the formless-sphere realm (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie there.
In the unincluded (apariyāpanna) [sphere], neither the underlying tendency to aversion nor the underlying tendency to conceit underlies.
Or, where the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*) does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) does not underlie?

In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to aversion does not fail to underlie there. In the unperturbed [states] (*apariyāpanna*), neither the underlying tendency to conceit nor the underlying tendency to aversion underlies.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*) …pe… the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) does not underlie?
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), and in the form-sphere (rūpadhātu) and formless-sphere (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) does not underlie there,

but the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) does not fail to underlie there. In the unincluded (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to aversion nor the underlying tendency to doubt underlies there.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence not underlie there?

In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not [necessarily] underlie there either.

It does not underlie. In the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu) and in the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) nor the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) underlies there.
Or, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to aversion not underlie there as well?
In unpleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to aversion does not fail to underlie there.

In the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm and in the unperturbed (the form and formless realms), neither the underlying tendency to lust for existence nor the underlying tendency to aversion underlies.
Wherever the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie there?
In the two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), and in the form-sphere (rūpadhātu) and the formless-sphere (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendency to aversion (paṭighānusaya) does not underlie;

yet, it is not the case that the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) does not underlie there either. In the unincluded (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to aversion nor the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to views... pe ...the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie?

In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie there, but the underlying tendency to doubt does not not underlie there (i.e., it does underlie). In the unperturbed (i.e., the supramundane), neither the underlying tendency to conceit nor the underlying tendency to doubt underlies there.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie?

In two feelings of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu), the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) does not fail to underlie there.
In painful feeling and in the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to lust for existence nor the underlying tendency to conceit underlies.
Wherever the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) not underlie there?

In regard to painful feeling, the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie there, but the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie there. In the unincluded (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to conceit nor the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies there.
Or, where the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie there? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to views does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to doubt not underlie there? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to views does not underlie? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to views … [and so on] … the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie? Yes.
Or, where the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie?

In the three feelings of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), the underlying tendency to attachment to existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) does not underlie there, yet the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) does not fail to underlie there either. In the unconditioned (*apariyāpanna*), neither the underlying tendency to attachment to existence nor the underlying tendency to doubt underlies there.
Wherever the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*) does not underlie? Yes.
Or conversely, wherever the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie? Yes.
Where the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie there?

In the three feelings of the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), the underlying tendency to lust for existence does not underlie, but the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie there. In the unincluded (*apariyāpanna*) [realms], neither the underlying tendency to lust for existence nor the underlying tendency to ignorance underlies. Or conversely:
where the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, does the underlying tendency to lust for existence not underlie there? Yes, it does. (The section based on a single root.)
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to conceit not underlie there?

In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to conceit does not fail to underlie there.
In the unincluded [sphere], the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion...
Where the underlying tendency to conceit does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also not underlie there?
In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust do not underlie; however, the underlying tendency to aversion does not [not underlie] there.

It does not underlie. In the unincluded (apariyāpanna), the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusaya) does not underlie there, and the underlying tendencies to sensual lust (kāmarāgānusaya) and aversion (paṭighānusaya) do not underlie there either.

Where the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to views (diṭṭhānusaya)…pe… the underlying tendency to doubt (vicikicchānusaya) not underlie there?
In the fine-material element (rūpadhātu) and the immaterial element (arūpadhātu), the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion do not underlie there, but [the others may].

Therein, the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie. In the non-included [states], the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, and the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie.
Or, wherever the underlying tendency to doubt does not underlie, there the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie? Yes.

Wherever the underlying tendency to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*) and the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*) not underlie there?

In the fine-material element (*rūpadhātu*) and the immaterial element (*arūpadhātu*), the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to existence does not fail to underlie there.
In the unconditioned (*apariyāpanna*), the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion...
And where the underlying tendency to attachment to existence does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and aversion also not underlie there?

In painful feeling, the underlying tendency to attachment to existence and the underlying tendency to sensual lust do not underlie; yet it is not that [the underlying tendency to aversion] does not underlie there.

The underlying tendency to aversion does not underlie it. In two types of feeling within the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), neither the underlying tendency to lust for existence nor the underlying tendency to aversion underlies them;

yet, the underlying tendency to lust for sense-pleasures does not fail to underlie them there. In the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), neither the underlying tendency to lust for existence nor the underlying tendencies to lust for sense-pleasures and aversion underlie it.
Where the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, does the underlying tendency to ignorance not underlie there?

In the fine-material element and the immaterial element, the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion do not underlie, yet the underlying tendency to ignorance does not fail to underlie there.
In the unperturbed (the supramundane), the underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to aversion... [do not underlie].
And where ignorance does not underlie, the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie.
Or, conversely, where the underlying tendency to ignorance does not underlie, do the underlying tendencies to sensual lust and to aversion not underlie there? Yes. (The Section Based on Pairs.
